units.function: A 2,913-line mixed unit/real-Git suite covering local workspace identity guards, Git-worktree base readiness, credential scrubbing, push preflight, low-trust sandbox isolation, workspace reuse/config freshness, task-session reset/fingerprints, comment wake batching, explicit provider session resume, session-state poisoning defenses, warnings, candidate ordering, compaction and sync-conflict classification.
units.dependencyDirection: Tests many helpers exported from the monolithic Heartbeat service plus Codex codec, filesystem/Git, Agent/workspace/trust shapes. The application layer directly knows local paths, adapter names, Git, provider session formats, Skill keys and internal metadata keys.
units.keyDataModels: Resolved and persisted ExecutionWorkspace; ProjectWorkspace and Git strategy; low-trust boundary/root Issue; versioned workspace/session config fingerprints and safe change categories; TaskSession params/display/lastRun; wake context/comment IDs; provider codec; session compaction policy.
units.lifecycle: Fail local Git-sensitive execution on workspace/project/path/providerRef/branch/metadata mismatch; reject invalid worktree bases and surface materialization cause; redact Git URL credentials; require an explicit PR-workflow Skill and push remote; fail low-trust non-sandbox work before workspace side effects; migrate only matching fallback sessions; fingerprint effective workspace/session configuration, reuse/refresh/replace deterministically and fail explicit restore loudly; reset or defer sessions by wake/config changes; strip control-plane metadata before adapter invocation; validate provider resume state and discard poisoned Hermes identifiers.
units.testAssessment: More than one hundred focused cases encode unusually rich operational lessons: fail-before-side-effect low-trust checks, explicit Skill capability rather than issue-text inference, fallback-cause fidelity, safe config category receipts, instruction content drift without content retention, no raw secret/env values in fingerprints, immutable explicit reuse, provider codec validation and poison fallback. The suite is nevertheless a 2,913-line architectural catch-all with extensive vendor and filesystem assumptions. Missing or weak areas include remote Connector attestation, cross-platform paths/Git, symlink/path traversal, push authorization rather than mere remote presence, config fingerprint canonicalization compatibility, collision/version migration, general session validation for non-Hermes adapters, data-retention/privacy policy, concurrent reuse, and end-to-end enforcement of all pure helpers.
units.designRationale: A Run may reuse mutable workspace and provider session state only when their effective configuration and identity still match. Low-trust work must be sandboxed before any host mutation, and persisted metadata should detect relevant drift without storing secret values or instruction contents.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs vendor-neutral execution-context freshness and containment across managed/local Connectors: exact workspace/data snapshot, trust boundary, secret/version changes, model/Skill configuration and opaque provider sessions must not silently cross responsibility contracts.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the invariant catalogue, safe category fingerprints, fail-before-side-effect low-trust gate, explicit capability preflight, immutable explicit reuse and codec-based session validation. Split ownership into WorkspacePort, TrustPolicyPort, SessionPort and Connector compatibility tests. Bind fingerprints to Work/accountable human/authority/data/approval/Skill/Connector versions; use opaque resource IDs instead of host paths; require remote attestation for non-local execution; keep vendor session parsing entirely in adapters and never persist private reasoning.
units.responsibilityConflict: Non-local execution bypasses the local Git guard without a tested remote attestation contract; a configured push remote is treated as capability without proving credential scope or human approval; low-trust policy is rooted in Issue ancestry but not a data-authorization/export contract. Non-Hermes arbitrary session IDs are accepted unchanged, and core Heartbeat logic contains vendor-specific session/compaction policy. Several warnings and decisions are English strings rather than stable codes, while automatic workspace/session migration is not tied to explicit accountable-human acceptance.
